topic: Microsoft DP-600 Implementing Analytics Solutions Using Microsoft Fabric certification exam preparation - maintaining a Fabric analytics solution, preparing data in lakehouses/warehouses, and implementing/managing semantic models with Power BI, SQL, KQL, DAX, and Copilot in Fabric
cert_name: Microsoft Certified: Fabric Analytics Engineer Associate
exam_format: Approximately 40-60 items (commonly ~48 standalone questions plus ~11 case-study questions), 100 minutes, passing score 700/1000, delivered at Pearson VUE test centers or online-proctored via OnVUE. Question types include multiple choice (single and multi-answer), fill-in-the-blank, drag-and-drop, and case studies. Associate-level certification renews annually via a free online Microsoft Learn assessment. Microsoft frequently runs free/discounted vouchers tied to Fabric events. The exam fee is approximately USD 165 and varies by region; present any fee as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current Microsoft pricing.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple response clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE', plus case-study scenario questions grounded in a described Fabric workspace
audience: Analytics engineers, Power BI developers, and BI/data professionals building analytics solutions on Microsoft Fabric. Candidates should be comfortable with data modeling and querying using SQL, basic KQL, and DAX, and with transforming and loading data. Some familiarity with the Fabric/Power BI ecosystem is assumed. A strong data-and-AI companion to the Microsoft AI catalog (AI-901, AI-103, the AB Copilot series) already in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Maintain a data analytics solution
domains.notes: Governing and operating a Fabric analytics solution: workspace and item configuration, access control and permissions (workspace roles, item permissions, OneLake data access roles), and applying security - row-level, column-level, object-level, and dynamic data masking - across lakehouses, warehouses, and semantic models. Lifecycle management: version control with Git integration, deployment pipelines across dev/test/prod, and Fabric CI/CD. Managing capacity, monitoring, and the admin/tenant settings that affect analytics workloads. Choosing the correct governance, security, or deployment control for a described Fabric scenario.

domains.name: Prepare data
domains.notes: The heaviest domain - the core analytics-engineering work. Getting and transforming data: ingesting with Dataflows Gen2, pipelines, notebooks, and shortcuts into OneLake; building lakehouses and warehouses; transforming with T-SQL, PySpark/Spark notebooks, and KQL (Real-Time Intelligence) as appropriate. Querying and analyzing: writing performant T-SQL and DAX, using the SQL analytics endpoint, and star-schema modeling. Copilot in Fabric is woven through here as an AI accelerator - using Copilot to help generate and explain transformations, DAX, and queries (while verifying the output). Choosing the right Fabric tool (Dataflow Gen2 vs notebooks/Spark vs pipelines; lakehouse vs warehouse) and technique for a described data-prep requirement.

domains.name: Implement and manage semantic models
domains.notes: Designing and optimizing Power BI semantic models on Fabric: choosing a storage mode (Direct Lake vs Import vs DirectQuery) and understanding Direct Lake behavior; building relationships, calculation groups, and DAX measures; large-model and composite-model considerations; performance tuning (aggregations, Vertipaq/DAX optimization, incremental refresh). Managing and securing models (row-level security, model permissions) and enabling report developers. Choosing the correct storage mode, modeling pattern, or optimization for a described analytics workload.

extra_guidance: DP-600 (Microsoft Fabric Analytics Engineer Associate) was Microsoft's fastest-growing certification and is the anchor of the modern Power BI + Fabric career path. MARKETING ANGLE: 'go from Power BI to end-to-end analytics engineering on Microsoft Fabric - with Copilot AI woven in.' The THREE domain names and weight ranges above are Microsoft's CURRENT skills-measured outline (the April 20, 2026 three-domain revision that REPLACED the older four-domain 'Plan/Prepare/Implement/Maintain' outline) - use the three-domain version verbatim and note many older blogs still quote the retired four-domain split. Use EXACT current Microsoft Fabric terminology: Microsoft Fabric, OneLake, lakehouse, warehouse, the SQL analytics endpoint, Dataflows Gen2, data pipelines, notebooks/Spark (PySpark), Real-Time Intelligence/KQL, semantic models, Power BI, DAX, Direct Lake vs Import vs DirectQuery, deployment pipelines, Git integration, and Copilot in Fabric - with a one-line note that Fabric evolves fast, so verify against current docs. The AI angle is Copilot in Fabric: show WHERE Copilot accelerates data prep, DAX/measure authoring, and query generation, and stress verifying Copilot output. This course DOES involve query languages (T-SQL, DAX, some KQL/PySpark) at a READ-AND-UNDERSTAND level - explain snippets rather than require live coding, and keep the focus on choosing the right Fabric tool/technique. Labs are read-and-understand Fabric walkthroughs (build a lakehouse and load with Dataflow Gen2, transform in a notebook, model a star schema, pick Direct Lake vs Import, write a DAX measure, apply row-level security, set up a deployment pipeline). Practice questions MUST include CASE-STUDY-style scenarios (the exam has ~11) plus standalone items: lakehouse vs warehouse, Dataflow Gen2 vs notebooks vs pipelines, Direct Lake vs Import vs DirectQuery, RLS/OLS/CLS choices, and performance-tuning decisions. NEVER promise a pass or use the word 'guarantee' in ANY form (Udemy compliance) - use 'exam-focused preparation' framing throughout, including learning objectives and who-this-is-for. Present the exam fee as approximate (~USD 165, varies by region), note the annual free renewal and Fabric free-voucher offers, and advise verifying current Microsoft pricing. The final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 100-minute time-management strategy INCLUDING case-study pacing. Scan the practice bank for stray other-vendor terms (AWS/Google/NVIDIA) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
